change_summary: The journal retracted the paper. An institutional investigation found the data in Figures 2 to 4 had been fabricated, and the notice says the conclusions cannot be relied on. The paper's results section presents its accuracy results in Figures 2 to 4.
evaluation: Your Introduction cites Brown and Kim [3] as showing that 200 mg of caffeine improves working memory by 12%, which is why you chose a 200 mg dose. The stored paper reports that 12% improvement at 200 mg, and it presents its accuracy results in Figures 2 to 4. The journal has retracted the article, and the notice says the data in Figures 2 to 4 had been fabricated and the conclusions cannot be relied on. This is the only citation of the paper in your draft, but your dose choice rests on it, so the impact on you is high.
recommendation: The journal has retracted the article, and the notice says the data in Figures 2 to 4 had been fabricated and the conclusions cannot be relied on. Your Introduction cites Brown and Kim [3] as showing that 200 mg of caffeine improves working memory by 12%, which is why you chose a 200 mg dose. Remove or replace this citation and re-check the claim it supported. Discuss the dose choice with your co-authors or supervisor, since the rationale for it rests on a retracted paper.
